contract_counterexamples.dependency: A successful revocation/demotion or queued pre-free operation can still precede pending reference and RCU finalizers. The report separates revoke success from later eligible deletion and physical page/IOMMU/cache release.

contract_counterexamples.contract_failure: A clock/quantum/IPI issuance/disable is not an independent finite all-finalizer progress contract. These are static permissible dependency states, not an observed hang.
contract_counterexamples.dependency: RCU needs relevant CPUs to reach quiet/update paths, actual timer/IPI handling, scheduled callback work and released partner/cross-CPU references. The described interface admits logical disable/recall while deferred work remains; no reviewed bound requires those dependencies to finish before a chosen deadline.

contract_counterexamples.contract_failure: A local CLOSED/ID absence/env eligibility flag cannot attest all provider queues/writers, account restitution, CPU/PD/RCU debt or physical backing settlement.
contract_counterexamples.dependency: Provider close may remain PENDING; client IDs can be discarded while provider work remains; quota reversal can fail separately. Retirement eligibility checks linker/log/binary state and explicitly omits CPU state.

contract_counterexamples.dependency: Reviewed worker paths include unsupported cancellation, indefinite completion waits and conditional timed join/free eligibility. Kernel capability revocation does not by itself replace these provider completion interfaces or prove storage/worker backing released.
